title: Inquiry expectations
description: Derived from design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 1.2 (Draft); the document wins. Proposal: Tillman Heisner accepts, changes or replaces it (Evaluation interfaces, section 4). What the inquiry agent's questions for one item should cover (section 4.5). The required mode (section 4.1 rule 12) sets the keys: mode A uses issue ids of the frozen issues (must_ask, must_not_ask, optional groups, question_count); mode B uses must-ask topics keyed by (source anchor, field, kind) (sections 2.2 and 4.5).
$comment: Derived from design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 1.2 (Draft); the document wins. Section 4.1 rule 4 leaves the file format (CSV, JSON or another) to the builder; this file describes the JSON form. Key names that section 4 does not give are marked 'Proposed name' in their description. A file holds the fields of its mode only (section 4.1 rule 12): mode A, must_ask, must_not_ask and question_count, with optional groups; mode B, must_ask_topics. A topic's anchor is anchor_xpath plus anchor_label as in the expected-value table (section 4.2), and its field the path below the anchored object; a document-level pointer that lies in no anchored object, such as /creators, is kept as the field, with no anchor. The scorer maps each question's tagged issue ids to topics through the draft's evidence entries (section 4.1 rule 12); a tag it cannot map, or maps to several topics, goes to the review list, never scored silently. Unwanted and mixed questions in mode B are counted against the step that let their issue through, never against the inquiry agent (section 2.2, D33 A); this file holds no row for them. Not expressed here: that min is at most max in question_count, and that the must_ask ids exist in the item's packet and the must_not_ask ids in the item's frozen report. Software filters the report before the inquiry agent sees it (design/HANDOFFS.md 2.4; design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 3.5), so must_not_ask tests the filter, not the agent. Corrected in phase P7 as design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md 1.1, section 10.8, proposes.

item_id.description: The item the file is for (4.1 rule 1).

variant_id.description: The variant the file is for (4.1 rule 1).

input_files.description: Proposed name. The input-side files the expected file was built for, each with its SHA-256 (4.1 rule 1). If a checksum no longer matches, the scorer skips the item and reports it.

evaluation_interfaces_version.description: Proposed name. The version of design/EVALUATION_INTERFACES.md the file follows (4.1 rule 1).

expected_file_version.description: Proposed name. The version of this expected file; a reviewed finding goes into a new version, and scores name it (4.1 rule 5).

canary.description: Only if canaries are adopted (5.3): the file's canary, random and at least 32 characters long. Option CS7, a canary in every row, would add a row field.

mode.description: The evaluation mode whose keys the file uses (section 4.1 rule 12): A, issue ids of the item's frozen issues; B, topics keyed by (source anchor, field, kind).

must_ask.description: Mode A. Issue ids that at least one question must tag.

must_not_ask.description: Mode A. Issue ids of the item's frozen report that no question may tag (section 4.5); they never reach the packet, so this list tests the report filter, not the agent.

groups.description: Mode A, optional. Sets of issue ids expected in one question; reported, not required.

question_count.description: Mode A. The accepted range of the question count, for example 8 to 14.

must_ask_topics.description: Proposed name. Mode B. The topics every correct pipeline must ask, keyed by (anchor, field, kind) (2.2).

allOf.$comment: Section 4.1 rule 12 and section 4.5, mode A: issue ids of the item's frozen issues.
Section 4.1 rule 12 and section 4.5, mode B: must-ask topics keyed by (source anchor, field, kind); no issue ids.

issue_id.description: An issue id: ISS-001 and so on (Issue format 4). Written by software, never by an agent.

sha256.description: A SHA-256 checksum: 64 hexadecimal characters, computed by software (Evaluation interfaces 3.1).

input_file.description: One input-side file the expected file was built for, with its checksum (4.1 rule 1). Field names from Evaluation interfaces 3.1.

topic.description: A must-ask topic: ASK-REQ and ASK fields the input does not state, and the expected source conflicts (2.2), keyed by (source anchor, field, kind) (4.1 rule 12).

anchor_xpath.description: The input element the object comes from, as in the expected-value table (4.2). Absent for a document-level field.

anchor_label.description: Blank for structured anchors; for a methodology anchor, a short label that tells objects of one type apart (4.2).

field.description: The path below the anchored object; for a document-level pointer that lies in no anchored object, the pointer itself, for example /creators (4.1 rule 12).

allOf.$comment: Section 4.1 rule 12: a document-level pointer is kept as it is, with no anchor.
